content:
Vice President JD Vance six weeks before the election sent a message to voters, attempting to whitewash the Trump administration's high prices.

In an interview with Newsmax's Greg Kelly, Vance said: "The message I want to deliver is very simple, mainly two points. First, do not hand power to those crazy people who created these problems in the first place."

He added: "If you feel troubled because of high prices, you absolutely have reason to feel troubled because of high prices."

The vice president's remarks are part of the Trump administration's more than twenty-month-long blame-shifting act, with government officials continuously attributing the country's current economic predicament to the Oval Office's former occupant.

However, since President Trump himself is one of the former occupants, the latest polls show that Americans are not buying this blame-shifting script. Meanwhile, data shows that inflation——pushed by the president's unwanted war of choice in Iran——has already offset wage growth.

Gas prices are $1.29 more per gallon than a year ago, and according to AAA data, diesel prices hit new highs again on Tuesday.

Critics on social media seized on Vance's mention of voters being "troubled" by high prices, believing that what Vance was actually talking about was his own "out-of-control" administration.

Another user @lisa_liberal found this clip highly promising, writing: "This should be the Democrats' ad, 5...4...3..."

Former Democratic National Committee chair Donna Brazile also used this clip to take aim at the Trump administration.

She wrote on X: "Those crazy people stirred up tariff disputes with our allies and fought a war of choice with no strategy for ending it. I think everyone has had enough of this madness."
